review: Independent source-informed B02 G3 implementation contract review v3
scope: Preimplementation review of G3 contract v3 against the approved B02 plan, prior G3 reviews and locally pinned Authlib source. No product or test code was reviewed or authored.

reviewed_points.assessment: The revised contract retains the approved B02/REQ-13 authentication foundation without claiming corporate SSO, AT-21 or G6 acceptance. The different-origin endpoint policy is now constrained by exact configured method/full-URL allowlists, TLS for real mode, no metadata-selected targets, no redirects and no environment proxy.

The proposed bounded retention policy resolves the unbounded-login-row finding in principle: expired-only deletion in batches of 1000, a 1024-row login admission ceiling under the same advisory lock, 60-second default maintenance, no deletion of unexpired states or pre-expiry revoked sessions, and DELETE rights limited to the two authentication tables. The plan preserves migration 001 and confines the authority delta to migration 002; the contract explicitly requires new migration, privilege, concurrency and lifecycle tests.

The catch-all OAuth-error classification is narrowed to named token endpoint error codes, and OAuth descriptions remain private. invalid_grant is appropriately treated as an invalid or expired authorization code.

The contract preserves direct AsyncOAuth2Client PKCE/token APIs, explicit configured issuer/audience and algorithm policy, Authlib CodeIDToken verification, strict NumericDate prechecks, bounded identity-encoded response streams, and actual service log-canary tests. The exact exp boundary and non-bool finite numeric checks address the pinned library's weaker predicate. No product/test result is implied by this plan review.

blockers.finding: The contract maps token-endpoint `invalid_request` 400/401 to 401 AUTH_REQUIRED. Under OAuth token endpoint semantics, invalid_request reports a malformed or incomplete token request, which is generated by this service from fixed parameters. The end-user's bad, expired, or mismatched authorization code is represented by invalid_grant. Therefore invalid_request generally indicates a server integration/configuration defect or provider protocol problem, not an authentication failure. The approved B02 plan makes callback state/token/nonce/code failures AUTH_REQUIRED and IdP communication failures DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE; it does not classify malformed server-generated token requests as user auth failures.
blockers.required_resolution: Map token-exchange invalid_grant to 401 AUTH_REQUIRED. Map invalid_request and other token-endpoint OAuth protocol/configuration/server errors to 503 DEPENDENCY_UNAVAILABLE, while keeping all provider descriptions and raw responses out of DTOs/logs. Add separate tests for invalid_grant versus invalid_request/server errors.

limitations: This is contract review only. No product, test, database, service or provider behavior was executed or accepted.

The GC design must still be checked in implementation for migration ownership, bounded row-lock behavior, exact transaction advisory lock identity, no private exception logging and shutdown cancellation; the contract supplies test oracles for those points.
